# `aitbc messaging subscribe`

Poll a topic for new messages (cursor polling — there is no push stream). Yields rows strictly newer than --from-cursor; without a cursor it starts at the current head (no backlog). Each poll prints the new rows plus the ``next_cursor`` marker to resume from. This is the agent-facing durable subscribe path (MSG-15) — the same kernel the SDK's ``MessagingClient.subscribe`` uses.

## Usage

```bash
aitbc messaging subscribe [OPTIONS] TOPIC
```

## Arguments

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `topic` | text | yes | — |

## Options

| Option | Type | Default | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `--from-cursor` | text | — | no | Resume after a <height>:<tx_hash> marker |
| `--follow` | flag | `false` | no | Keep polling (default: one poll then exit) |
| `--interval` | float | `5.0` | no | Seconds between polls when --follow |
| `--max-polls` | integer | — | no | Bound the poll count even with --follow |
| `--limit` | integer | `50` | no | Rows fetched per poll (server caps at 100) |
| `--rpc-url` | text | — | no | Blockchain RPC URL |

## Examples

```bash
aitbc messaging subscribe TOPIC
RPC_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8202/rpc
aitbc messaging subscribe TOPIC --rpc-url "$RPC_URL"
```
